**RESUME HERE -- 2026-09-17 night, THIRD fold, correcting doing 56 which went stale inside three minutes: ic is NOT idle, and its next action is a question to vc.** hv has named the next release 3.1.0 (hv decision 24, 2026-09-17 19:01Z, read on hv's own board and stated in intent/wip.md line 21, a minor because ST0076 adds a verb and an index level rather than repairing something shipped broken). THE RELEASE-DOC WORK IS LANDED: `intent/docs/releasing.md` and the CLAUDE.md pointer went in at 8afcca8d6 on vc's ruling, in one commit, from the BANKED text read back with `git cat-file` rather than from a working copy, with vc's three conditions held -- the baseline section stays OPEN and addressed to hv, the staleness check stays banked and unbuilt, and the pointer is in CLAUDE.md itself and not the template. The only difference between the banked text and what landed is the pre-commit formatter's table padding, verified by diff. ic has NO assigned work outstanding: ask vc before starting anything. Doing 55 named the 0439 reproduction as ic's next step; it was run and accepted hours before this replaced it, which is the defect dc named across three nodes tonight -- a resume item describing completed work is worse than none, because it is confidently wrong in the one place a fresh context trusts without checking. **0441 IS FINISHED END TO END:** code c649596ef at its own patch-id 2e611147, close 98c580d12, docs/reference d21550ae5, and the behavioural proof is run-d3, ACCEPTED by vc at the scope claimed and no wider -- under identical conditions with the daemon PROVEN watching, the observable harm is gone and an estate that used to end skewed now ends clean. d2 read WARNINGS 1 with a closing doctor of 1 finding (residue: view-skew); d3 read WARNINGS 0 with a closing doctor of 0, on identical opening and closing populations, and the window was tested rather than assumed (d2's ingest fired 3.7 s INTO the burst, and d3's observation window was the longer of the two). vc's word is that all three installed-pair runs are now done. The run record is banked at refs/bank/ic/0441/d3.md and carries the reasoning, the asymmetry (zero disk.sync_from_disk is the fix's PREDICTED observation, not an absence of evidence -- vc's correction of my own first write-up), and the readings that must not be cited. **THE INSTRUMENT IS HARDENED AND RE-BANKED** at refs/bank/ic/0441/verify.sh: it records realpath, sha256 and mtime of the binary at BOTH ends of a run and refuses the verdict if they differ, because `intent` on PATH is a symlink into this checkout's own target/release and any rebuild swaps it mid-flight (watchout 82, which now also carries hv decision 23 on ungated Rust dependency bumps). All four arms were driven, not merely written. The UNHARDENED script that actually produced d3 is preserved beside it at verify-as-run-d3.sh so the run's provenance survived the re-bank, with probe_registry.py. dc independently hashed the same artefact during the AC-06.2 drive and it matches over every character dc quoted, so dc's drive and d3 share a PROVABLE subject rather than two readings of one version string. **THE RELEASE-DOC WORK IS BANKED AND IS NOT ic's TO LAND:** refs/bank/ic/releasing/doc is `intent/docs/releasing.md` on the internal shelf (vc ruled the location), staleness-check is the proposal that the cut REFUSE a stale docs/reference rather than a page asking someone to remember (explicitly not built, and blocked on the baseline ruling below), and claude-md.patch adds the index pointer and applied clean at banking time. It landed at 8afcca8d6 with no ordering dependency on cc's release notes, vc having ruled that a process document and a release's notes do not touch. What the document establishes, and the reason it was worth writing: `build release` commits the version bump (bin/.devbin/cmd/build.d/release:1171), tags the commit it just made (:1221) AND pushes main and the tag to both remotes (:1240, :1242), so there is no window after the tag by any sequencing, a cut is NOT reversible up to the push, the driver cannot be run from a tool session at all while NO PUSH stands, and the regeneration must therefore be committed BEFORE the driver runs. v3.0.3 does not contain its own reference pages -- tag 46599d145, regeneration a87a94a4a twenty-four minutes later, and --is-ancestor says no -- so anyone checking out that tag reads the previous cut's surface. **THE ONE OPEN ITEM IS hv's:** which release the reference pages measure presence against. The tool default is v3.0.0 and has never moved; the last two regenerations both passed v3.0.1 by hand, mine among them, copied from the previous invocation rather than applied from a rule; v3.0.2 and v3.0.3 both shipped on 2026-09-14; a register exists at every 3.0.x tag, so any would work. Under every reading of the convention today's pages are at least one release behind. vc is putting it to hv as its own question rather than stacking it on the five rulings hv had already given.

**MUST NOT, and these are here because a positive list cannot carry them and nobody can discover them from one.** Do NOT invent the baseline rule -- that section of the document stays OPEN and addressed to hv, and its credibility rests on ic owning the miniature version of the same mistake. Do NOT re-land or re-edit `intent/docs/releasing.md` to fill in the baseline section: it is landed at 8afcca8d6 with that section deliberately OPEN, and an answer nobody gave is worse than a question plainly asked. Do NOT remove wt-0441 or its target dir: vc ruled they STAY and go at the close-out rather than at the end of this run, because removal is the one step in the sequence that cannot be re-run, and the d3 residual is exactly what a second look would want them for. Do NOT build an instrumented reading of the render path -- vc ruled against it because 0441's own arm `a_sync_writes_no_render_the_store_has_moved_past` already proves the MECHANISM, d3 was only ever the integration reading, and a second instrument re-proving what a cheaper one proved is the overtesting hv has ruled against twice. Do NOT put the CLAUDE.md pointer into lib/templates/llm/_CLAUDE.md: it has no such section, the index lives in CLAUDE.md's preserved user:start/user:end region, and that template IS in DIRT_SCOPE, so the reflex would stale the pair for all four nodes to land a documentation pointer. Do NOT cite store-versus-canon byte equality as evidence in any canon-guard run: it read EQUAL in d2, where the overwrite demonstrably happened, so it discriminates nothing and would make a report sound stronger while being worse.

**THIS ITEM REPLACED DOING 56 BECAUSE ONE OF ITS OWN CONDITIONS WAS ALREADY DISCHARGED WHEN IT WAS COMMITTED**, hv having named 3.1.0 two hours earlier -- the mild form of the very defect the fold was fixing, in the same hour, to a node that had just been shown the class. What limited the damage was the FORM and not the care: it was written as a condition ("until hv names the version") rather than as a state ("hv has not named the version"), and a condition is checkable by whoever reads it while a state is simply believed. See watchout 83. **PEER STATE AND OPEN ISSUES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED HERE.** They rot on a board faster than anything else and a stale line is multiplied by the number of readers rather than divided by it; read them live with `intent st list`, `intent issues list` and `intent wb status`. NO RELEASE, NO PUSH.
